trials.notes: Passed 8/8. Correctly uses WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), walks tokens with next_token(), restricts matches to #text, compares decoded get_modifiable_text(), and wraps serialize_token() output. All HTML API methods used are documented, with no _doing_it_wrong records. Its parser-error fallback is also reasonable because it preserves accumulated output if normalize() cannot produce a full serialization.

Passed 8/8. Uses the right processor and the documented token-rewrite pattern: #text guard, decoded get_modifiable_text(), and serialize_token() inside literal <mark> wrappers. All HTML API calls are documented and execution recorded no misuse. Minor caveat: on unsupported-parser error, normalize($html) ?? $html can return raw original input, discarding prior wrappers and normalization; this did not affect the frozen cases.

Passed 8/8. Same correct documented pattern as trial 2, with a clear #text-only check that avoids comments, attributes, and special-element opener text. All HTML API calls are documented and no _doing_it_wrong records appear. Same minor fallback caveat: if normalize() returns null after get_last_error(), returning raw input is not a normalized token rewrite.

failure_analysis: No trial failed any frozen hidden case; all three passed 8/8. The docs succeeded by making four contracts visible: use WP_HTML_Processor, not the Tag Processor, for fragment structure and normalized output; use create_fragment() for body fragments; ordinary text is only #text tokens, while comments and special text-bearing elements can also have modifiable text; and token rewrites should inspect decoded get_modifiable_text() but emit serialize_token(). The entity-encoded case was handled because get_modifiable_text() documents decoded text. The split-text, attribute, comment, and special-element risks were avoided because the docs explicitly warn not to treat every token with modifiable text as ordinary DOM text. Near-miss: all candidates invented get_last_error() fallbacks. Trial 2 and 3 chose a raw-input fallback if normalize() fails, which would lose normalization and earlier wrappers on unsupported markup; the docs warn about this, but the fallback decision remains easy to get subtly wrong.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain that normalize() and raw input discard accumulated token-rewrite output, but candidates still diverged on parser-error fallback policy.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact fallback decision table for token rewrites: accumulated output, null/empty fail-closed, normalize(original), and raw original, with the consequence of each for normalization and retained edits.

doc_gaps.problem: The special-element contract is present but spread across narrative text. This task depended on knowing SCRIPT/STYLE/TITLE/TEXTAREA text is carried on opener tokens, not #text children.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small token taxonomy table showing ordinary #text, comments, and special-element openers, with whether get_modifiable_text() is decoded/raw and whether it should count as ordinary DOM text.

doc_gaps.problem: Incomplete trailing syntax and unsupported parser aborts are separate edge cases, but they are easy to conflate when writing a string-returning rewrite.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State directly that incomplete trailing syntax may be omitted by normalization and is checked with paused_at_incomplete_token(), while unsupported markup sets get_last_error() and may make normalize()/serialize() return null.
